    D12 · The setup panel becomes a drawer — and the builder’s four panels join the phone’s one sheet system (fold-in, your read of the build · 22 September)

    You asked whether the setup panel could open as a bottom drawer — “I think it will look better and likely be able to fit everything on screen too.” The first half is right and the second half is not, and the numbers are worth having before you rule. The panel is already bottom-anchored: it is pinned 92px above the foot, inset 14px each side, and capped so it scrolls inside itself. What it is missing is the drawer’s form — flush edges, an 18px top radius, a grab line, a dimmed page behind, and a title once the row that opened it is covered. Measured on the build today: a drawer’s room is 583px at 390×667 against the card’s 555px, and 760 against 732 at 390×844 — the change is worth 28px of height and 29px of width, and nothing else. The panel’s content is 566px, so at 844 it already fits with no scroll (568 tall, Generate at 640, Reshuffle at 693 — it fits even with Game rules expanded, 713 in 752) and at 667 it overflows by 11px, which is the clipping in your screenshot. A drawer alone lands that at 579 in 583 — it fits by four pixels, and only if the drawer is given no title. So the fit is a content decision, not a container one, and B trims the content as well.

    The real argument for the drawer is that this one screen now speaks two languages. Tapping a player’s position raises a proper drawer; tapping Setup, Templates, Print or a player’s number raises a floating card — captured side by side below, same screen, same width, same gesture. That is the inconsistency your eye caught. It is also why the scope is four panels and not one: converting Setup alone leaves three panels on the same screen behaving the old way, which reads worse than today because the inconsistency gets sharper rather than softer.

    ⚠ What is moving underneath this drawing, and is not being ruled here. The page behind the drawer is drawn as dev stood this morning, and it has already moved since — read the drawer, not its surroundings. Landed on dev today by two other sessions: the tool row above the grid is now five squares (Clear positions moved up out of the grid on your ruling); the status strip is reframed; and the Setup row has lost its lime wash and instead carries a one-tap Auto-fill pill while a game has no lineup (their rule, in its accurate form: a lime pill is the one thing you can do in ONE TAP — when the next step needs a decision rather than a tap it is a door, not a pill; the no-pill states are a clash, which routes through Review, already Ready, and an empty roster). That last one is not only cosmetic — see the question it raises below. Almost none of that shows here — at 390×667 the drawer covers everything below the team name (A leaves 16px of page visible, B leaves 73) — so read the drawer, not its surroundings. D12 and D13 rule the container and what is inside it; the row that opens it, the strip above it and the tool row are someone else’s decision and can change shape without changing anything drawn below.

    Design intent — what changes on the screen. Tapping the Setup row raises the same surface a player’s position already raises: full width, flush to the top of the bottom bar, an 18px top radius, a grab line you can tap to close, and the page behind dimmed. The bar stays visible and tappable beneath it, as it does under More — the builder is a page under the bar, not a dialog over it. B also trims the content, which is where the fit actually is: Innings to fill and Game rules fold together behind one quiet disclosure (both are per-game overrides of a default, and “1 to 6” is a row spent on a value almost nobody changes); the explainer drops to one line; and Reshuffle becomes a quiet row under Generate rather than a second full-width button competing with it. The drawer gains a title — “Lineup setup” — because once the scrim covers the row that opened it, nothing on screen says what this is; the position sheet titles itself with the player for the same reason. Two things I want you to weigh, not wave through. (1) The scrim hides the grid. Today the page behind is undimmed, so in principle you could watch the grid while changing Innings — in practice the card already covers 555 of 667px, so you cannot; at 844 you lose a genuine sliver. (2) Reshuffle gets quieter. It is a real action some coaches use every game; B demotes it to a text row. If you use it often, say so and it stays a button. Restyled the container — flush, radius, grab line, scrim — for Setup, Templates, Print and the player row menu New the drawer’s title row; the single “Innings to fill · Game rules” disclosure Unchanged every control’s words and behaviour, Generate’s position, the confirms on Regenerate and Reshuffle, the grid, and every width above 640 — the desktop keeps its popover exactly as it is.

    One question the Setup row’s rebuild hands to this decision, and I would rather ask it than quietly answer it. That session’s rule is a lime pill is the one thing you can do right now; no pill means there is nothing to do here — so a game with no lineup now generates from the row in one tap, without opening anything. Two consequences for the drawer. (1) Its job narrows, which strengthens B: for a new lineup the row already does the common thing, so the drawer is for the coach who wants to change something first — a reason to fold the rarely-touched controls away rather than stack them. (2) “Generate lineup” and “Reshuffle” inside the drawer are drawn in the same style — checked in the code, both are the portal’s secondary button — so the one action this surface exists for is indistinguishable from the optional thing under it. That is a defect on its own terms, independent of the lime question, and worth fixing whichever way you rule. ⚠ I had the reason for it wrong at first, and the correction matters more than the error. I wrote that a phone coach now has no primary action in this flow. Not true — Mark ready is a lime pill eight pixels above the Setup row whenever the lineup can be marked, and that is the point rather than a gap: the lime wash used to point a coach at Auto-fill — regenerate the thing you just built — while the real next step sat above it in the same colour. Two competing limes, and the louder one was the wrong answer. So the case for making Generate lime is not “the phone lost its primary”; it is simply that a panel’s one reason for existing should not look like its optional sibling. I have not changed it in either drawing — it is drawn exactly as it is built — because making it lime is a second ruling, not a detail of this one. Say the word and it becomes the lime pill in B, and the two surfaces speak the same language. Leaving it is also defensible: the row’s pill and the drawer’s button would then never be on screen together, since the pill is gone the moment a lineup exists.

It still fits a short phone with 25px spare and no scroll, which was the point; it is simply not the 61px of headroom the drawing promised.

    QA walk · stage 0 · The shell · ledger §208

    Walk the shell on a phone

    Twenty-two steps in five parts. Tick each one as you go (they are remembered on this device), give each part a verdict, and paste the summary back into the chat at the end. Do parts A–D on an actual phone — a browser window narrowed to 390px shows the shapes but not the thumb.

    Sign in as
    Wherehttp://localhost:3000 (the dev server) — on a phone, your machine’s LAN address on the same port
    Accountuat-coach@uat-test-org.local · the standing UAT password in .env.local (UAT_COACH_PASSWORD)
    TeamUAT Test Team (UAT Test Org, 2026 season) — the game-day fixture; UAT Between Seasons is the closed-season team for part E
    Widthsa phone (390-ish) for A–D; a desktop window (1200+) for B5 and C5

    A · More is a sheet

    1. On Overview, tap More. A sheet the full width of the phone rises from the bar, the page behind it dims, a small grab line sits at its top. No narrow popover on the right.
    2. The first row is Notifications with its count; then ONE Your teams list: UAT Test Team tinted with no chevron (you are here), and UAT Between Seasons on the same list with 2025 Season in small type at its right and a chevron — no second “No live season” header. (Changed on the walk, 20 Sep: the switcher had never been drawn; two headers over two rows cost 25px of the sheet.)
    3. Three tiles — Practice plans · Lineups · Skills & Goals. Tap each in turn; each opens its room in one tap and the sheet is gone.
    4. Below the tiles: Season (Tournaments) beside Progress (Insights); Money beside Communication (Email families); Team as four rows in two columns (Tryouts · Staff · Documents · Settings); Help · Sign out at the foot. Every label on one line — “Email families” included — and the side-by-side rows carry no chevron. Nothing scrolls inside the sheet on a 844-tall phone (a small scroll on a shorter one is fine). (Changed on the walk, 20 Sep: “Email families” wrapped at 390 and 360; the chevron on a half-width row was the 26px it needed — the word stays, the column gives.)
    5. Tap the dimmed page above the sheet — it closes. Tap More, then the ✕ in the bar — it closes. Every row is a comfortable tap; none feels short.

    B · One identity line

    1. Open Schedule. The bar at the top is ONE slim line — team name · record · the “?” — not the two-line block. The “?” is a whole disc inside the line, its top not sliced off by the screen edge. The page title sits right under it.     Walk the Schedule on a phone

    Thirty-five steps in six parts. Tick each one as you go (they are remembered on this device), give each part a verdict, and paste the summary back into the chat at the end. Do parts A–E on an actual phone — the slide, the pinned month name and the bottom sheet are the point, and a narrowed window has neither a thumb nor a foot to rise from. Part F is a desktop window and a tablet (or a window at ~750). Part C needs a game that has not started yet: the fixture's probe game is moved to thirty minutes ago every time a probe runs, so open a game on a future date for C — or ask the build session to nudge the probe game ahead first.

    Sign in as
    Wherehttp://localhost:3000 (the dev server) — on a phone, your machine’s LAN address on the same port
    Accountuat-coach@uat-test-org.local · the standing UAT password in .env.local (UAT_COACH_PASSWORD)
    TeamUAT Test Team (UAT Test Org, 2026 season) — seventeen dated events from April to October; the probe game is today's, the finished game is @ Lakeside in April
    Widthsa phone (390-ish) for A–E; a desktop window (1200+) and a tablet or a ~750 window for F

    A · The list

    1. Open Schedule. It opens on today: the month name (SEPTEMBER 2026) sits at the top of the list and today's row is directly under it — no scroll animation, nothing to wait for. Above the list there is only the title row; the List · Week · Month row is gone.
    2. The title row reads Schedule … [a list glyph] [+] — a 44px icon button beside the lime “+”, and the “+” has no chevron. Tap “+”: the same six-type menu as before (Tournament, Tournament game, League game, Practice, Team event).
    3. The rows share one white frame with a thin line between them — no card gaps, no grey. Each row is the name on the first line and the date and time beneath (“Sep 21 · 11:22 a.m.”); today's game keeps its Game day pill at the right.
    4. Slide up (into the past). The month name stays pinned at the top of the list as the rows pass under it, then the next month's name takes its place. The title row and the “+” never move; the page behind does not scroll.
    5. Slide down past the last row (October). “Export the season ›” sits under the list as a quiet row, then empty paper — the last month can reach the top. Tap the export row: the chooser opens with Calendar .ics (the phone's one export, as before).
    6. Tap the view glyph. A short menu of three rows — List ✓ · Week · Month — each with its glyph, the current one ticked. Tap the dimmed page or Escape: it closes. Open it again and pick Week: the menu closes and the glyph becomes the week glyph.
    7. Pick List again from the menu: the list lands on today again (not where you left it).
    8. Tap any row: the event sheet opens as before; back closes it and the list is where it was.

    B · Week and Month

    1. In Week: the ‹ › arrows are comfortable 44px taps and the range reads “Sep 21 – Sep 27, 2026”. A run of empty days is one quiet dashed line — “Tue 22 – Sat 26 · nothing scheduled” — and a day with something keeps its card exactly as before (the chip with its colour rail, the Game day pill under it on game day). No empty day cards.
    2. Press ‹ to a week with nothing on it: one line, “Mon 14 – Sun 20 · nothing scheduled”. Press › back.
    3. Pick Month. The grid shows a dot per event in the type's colour instead of cut-off words; today's number is ringed and today is already selected (filled); the numbers and the weekday heads are a step larger than before.
    4. Under the grid: a band naming the day — “Monday, September 21” — and today's rows in the list's own shape with a time lead (“11:22 a.m.” — the fixture's time moves day to day) and the Game day pill.
    5. Tap an empty day (the 22nd). The cell fills, the band reads “Tuesday, September 22” and one quiet line says Nothing on Tuesday, September 22. Tap a day with a dot: its rows appear. Tap a row: the sheet opens.
    6. Press › to October: the 1st is selected and its rows (or the quiet line) sit under the grid — never a day the grid does not show. Press ‹ back: today is selected again.

    C · The sheet before first pitch

    1. Open a game that has not started (see the note above). Under the title and the when-line, the where-row: pin · UAT Fields · 1 · Uniform: Home kit · chevron, a full-width 44px row. Tap anywhere on it — the map opens.
    2. Straight under the where-row: the Attendance · Lineup · Scouting tabs (44px tall) and then the attendance — no score door, no “Awards given” box, no Edit · Cancel · Delete above them.
    3. The attendance heading with All in · Reset beside it (44px taps); under it the five count chips as one row of five equal cells, the counts at a readable size. Tap a chip: the list filters; tap it again: all.
    4. The players are hairlined rows in the sheet — name on the left, the status badge (In · Late · Out · No reply) as the row's trail with its word at body size, a chevron — 48px each, no “Edit RSVP” button anywhere. Eight or more players fit on the first screen.
    5. Scroll to the foot of the list: + Add final score as a quiet door under the players (this is the not-started game’s order — the tabs lead before first pitch; on a game that has started the door is at the top, D2), then notes or links if the game has any. No “Season attendance” row anywhere on the sheet (it left on your 21 Sep read — likelier to leave the game by accident than to open Insights on purpose).
    6. At the very foot: Edit details · Cancel event · Delete as three equal cells under a thin line, Delete in red. Tap Delete: the confirmation takes the row's place; Cancel it.

    D · The sheet after first pitch

    1. Open the finished game (@ Lakeside, April, 2 – 7). Under the when-line the score leads: 2 – 7 LOSS with Edit score as a 44px pill and “Add to the book on Lakeside ›” as a 44px row beneath; then the Rivalry/Scrimmage chips if any; then Awards given with its 44px “Give an award”; then the tabs and the attendance.
    2. Open today's probe game (it has started on an ordinary visit — the fixture keeps it thirty minutes into the past): + Add final score sits right under the when-line — a pill drawn a little smaller than the where-row (36px tall) on a tap area that is still 44 (revised 21 Sep) — then Awards given with “Enter a final score to unlock awards”, then the tabs — the score is the job once the game is on.
    3. Tap + Add final score: the two fields and Save appear in the same place. Cancel.
    4. Open a practice (UAT probe practice): title · when · where-row · the Practice plan block with its 44px “Open the plan →” · then the attendance straight away (no tab row) · the foot row. Nothing about scores.
    5. On any game, open Lineup: “Edit in Lineups →” / “Build lineup →” is a 44px tap. Open Scouting: the book, as before.

    E · The RSVP sheet and the floor

    1. Tap a player's row. A bottom sheet rises from the foot of the screen over the dimmed event sheet: a grab line, the player's name, the day and the event, four full-width 52px choices — In · Late · Out · No reply — with the current one ticked and tinted, and the note field under them.
    2. Tap a different choice. The sheet closes at once, the row's badge reads the new word, and “Saving… → Saved” shows at the foot and fades. Tap the row again and set it back.
    3. Open the sheet, type a note, then tap the dimmed page: the sheet closes, the row shows the note flag, Saved fades. Open it again: the note is there. Clear it.
    4. Open the sheet and use the phone's back gesture (or Escape on a keyboard): the RSVP sheet closes and the event sheet stays open. Back again closes the event sheet.
    5. Nothing on the event sheet is a fiddly tap: tabs, All in · Reset, the five chips, the rows, Edit score, the book row, Give an award, the plan door, Edit in Lineups, the foot row, the where-row — every one a 44px target. The Out badge reads clearly on the white.

    F · Nothing moved on the desktop and at 768

    1. Desktop (1200+): Schedule opens in April, the List · Week · Month toggle and the Export button in their row above the list, the worded “+ Add Event ▾” with its chevron; the page scrolls as a page; no view glyph, no export row under the list.
    2. Desktop: Week is the seven columns; Month is the grid with its text chips and “+N more”; a cell's chip opens the event as before.
    3. Desktop: the event sheet keeps its order exactly — title, when, where line, the score door, Awards given, Edit · Cancel · Delete, then the tabs. The attendance rows are hairlined rows (no cards) and tapping a row opens the RSVP choices as a small centred dialog; the inline “Edit RSVP” editor is gone here too.
    4. Tablet or a ~750 window: the List · Week · Month toggle is a comfortable 44px; the sheet keeps the desktop order with every control at 44 (the map link included).

    QA walk · stage 3 · Game week · ledger §220 · built on dev 21 Sep 2026 · walk owed

    Walk the lineup builder on a phone

    Thirty-nine steps in eight parts. Tick each one as you go (they are remembered on this device), give each part a verdict, and paste the summary back into the chat at the end. Do parts A–F on an actual phone — the hold-to-drag, the pinned stepper and the bottom sheet are the point. Part G is the template editor on the phone; part H crosses the Schedule, the game-day console and the Overview, on the phone and on a desktop window. Two games: the fixture's UAT probe game (today, a saved lineup — moved to thirty minutes ago every time a probe runs, so its sheet reads as a game in play) and UAT probe game · no lineup (five days out, nothing decided — reseeded clean every run, so anything you generate on it is gone by the next seed).

    Sign in as
    Wherehttp://localhost:3000 (the dev server) — on a phone, your machine’s LAN address on the same port
    Accountuat-coach@uat-test-org.local · the standing UAT password in .env.local (UAT_COACH_PASSWORD)
    TeamUAT Test Team (UAT Test Org, 2026 season) — More → Lineups lists the games; the probe game is today's, the no-lineup game is next week's
    Widthsa phone (390-ish) for A–G; H adds a desktop window (1200+) and, if you have one, a tablet or a ~750 window

    A · The row

    1. More → Lineups → the UAT probe game. Under the status strip there is one row where Format · Innings · Auto-fill · Reshuffle used to be: “Everyone bats · 6 innings” with “Auto-fill · Balanced” beneath and a chevron at the right. White, a thin edge, about the height of a schedule row.
    2. The date line above reads “Mon, Sep 21 · time · View on schedule” on ONE line — no year.
    3. The first players are on screen without scrolling: two whole rows and the top of a third above the bar.

    B · The panel

    1. Tap the row. A panel rises above the bar: SETUP with Format and Innings side by side, then AUTO-FILL with Mode, Fill, Innings to fill, Game rules ▾ and the note, then Generate lineup and Reshuffle. The list behind does not move. The row's chevron has turned up.
    2. Change Innings to 7: the row behind now reads “Everyone bats · 7 innings”. Change the Mode to Competitive: the row's caption reads “Auto-fill · Competitive” and the A-squad choices appear in the panel. Put both back.
    3. Tap the dimmed page (or the phone's back gesture): the panel closes, nothing changed.
    4. Open the panel and tap Generate lineup. It asks to regenerate (this lineup has positions) — Regenerate. The panel closes, the list shows the new positions, “Saved” fades at the foot. Undo (part C) brings the old ones back.
    5. Open the panel and tap Reshuffle — Keep current on the question: the panel stays open. Ask again and confirm: the panel closes and the positions have changed.

    C · The tools

    1. Under the row: four squares — undo, redo, a printer, a templates glyph — left-aligned, each a comfortable tap. Undo and redo are dim until there is something to undo.
    2. Tap undo after the reshuffle: the positions go back; redo brings them forward.
    3. Tap the printer: the same Dugout poster / Batting order card panel as before with the Landscape · Portrait switch. Tap Dugout poster on a lineup with an open role: the “Print with open roles?” question — Keep working.
    4. Tap the templates glyph: today's template panel — the saved “Probe lineup template” row with its delete, and the “Save current lineup as a template” field. Close it.

    D · One inning at a time

    1. Under the tools: “‹ INNING 1 OF 6 · 9/9 ›” as a green pill between two arrow squares, and a row of six small dots beneath (the first filled with a ring, the others amber outlines — those innings still have an open role).
    2. Every player is one row: the batting number in its box, the name, then a small position, a boxed position, a small position. On inning 1 the small position on the LEFT is empty (there is no inning before), the box is inning 1's, the small one on the right is inning 2's.
    3. Tap ›. The pill reads “INNING 2 OF 6 · 8/9” (the 8/9 amber — a role is open), the ring moves to the second dot, and every row now shows inning 1 small on the left, inning 2 in the box, inning 3 small on the right. An open cell reads “—” with an amber edge. ‹ goes back; on inning 6 the › is dim and the right-hand small column is empty.
    4. Scroll down the list. The stepper and the dots stay pinned under the team name as the rows pass beneath them. Scroll back up.
    5. Tap the pill itself: the inning inspector opens on that inning (the same panel the grid's heading opened). Its “Inning 3 ›” steps it — and when you close it, the list is on inning 3 too.
    6. Hold a batting number for a moment: the row lifts. Drag it two rows down and let go: the order changes and the numbers renumber. Undo puts it back.
    7. Tap a batting number: the row's sheet — Move up · Move down · Remove from lineup · Cancel — as before. Move down, then Move up; Cancel.
    8. Tap the status strip's “Review ›” and, in the Lineup check, an inning row (“Inning 2 …”): the inspector opens on that inning and the list behind steps to it.
    9. Under the list: “Hold a number to move a player · ‹ › for the innings”, then Clear positions, then the not-in-the-lineup row with Add to lineup — all as before.

    E · The position sheet

    1. Tap a player's boxed position. A bottom sheet rises over the dimmed page: a grab line, the player's name, one line like “Inning 2 of 6 · playing SS · Bench in the 1st, 3B in the 3rd”, then Bench as a full-width row, then chips under BEST (in rank order, “1st · 2nd”; a pitcher's P with “2 of 4 used”), FINE — ANYWHERE NOT NEVER, NEVER in red, then OR · Leave open. The current position is filled and says “now”. No chevron anywhere on the row.
    2. Tap a different chip. The sheet closes at once, the box reads the new position, the small neighbours are unchanged, “Saved” fades. If the pick clashes with another player, the pill's edge turns red, the stepper pill reads “⚠ 2 share C” in red and that inning's dot goes red.
    3. Undo (the square): the position goes back; the clash clears.
    4. Open the sheet and tap a Never chip (Avery or Blake Test have none — pick a player with a red group, or skip): it applies without a question, in red on the chart's word. Undo.
    5. Open the sheet, tap Bench: the box reads Bench. Open it again and tap Leave open: the box reads “—” with the amber edge and the stepper's figure drops by one. Undo twice.
    6. Open the sheet and use the phone's back gesture (or the dimmed page): it closes, nothing changed, and the box you tapped is where the focus is.

    F · A new lineup

    1. More → Lineups → UAT probe game · no lineup (next week). The strip reads “Not started · Choose positions or Auto-fill to begin”, and the Setup row is lime — “Everyone bats · 9 innings / Auto-fill · Balanced” — with the four squares under it (undo and redo dim, the templates glyph live).
    2. The stepper reads “INNING 1 OF 9” with no figure, nine quiet outlined dots, and every player's box reads “—” with no amber edge (nothing is started, so nothing is open). Four whole players fit on the first screen.
    3. Tap the lime row → Generate lineup: no question (nothing to replace), the panel closes, every box fills, the first dot fills, the rest turn amber, the row stays lime until you leave the page (its tone is decided when the page opens, not as you work).
    4. Leave and come back: the row is white now (a lineup exists). The reseed will clear this game again.

    G · The template editor

    1. More → Lineups → Templates → Probe lineup template. The same Setup row (white — this template has positions), no tool squares (a template has no undo or print), the stepper — this template clashes in every inning, so the pill is red: “INNING 1 OF 6 · ⚠ 3 clashes” — and every dot red.

On a desktop window (1200+): the builder is the grid with Setup · Auto-fill · Reshuffle and the worded Templates ▾ exactly as before, the year in the date line; the Schedule sheet's Lineup tab keeps “Edit in Lineups →” at the foot, and gains the same ‹ inning › flip on the batting order.     The precedent, and how it actually played out

    Your stage 0 walk did not just confirm stage 0 — two things you raised on it became stage 1’s first two items, drawn ahead of the questions the plan already had. I expected the §220 walk to do the same to this list. It did not: the walk passed clean. The movement came from peer sessions drawing D12–D14 on the same screen in parallel — three rulings on one screen inside a day, while this stage was being drawn. Same lesson, different door — these five are the questions the plan already holds, and they are not a closed set.

    Not reopened

    Named so the ruling does not have to cover them.

    • The four primary tabs, and the More sheet.
    • The descriptor vocabulary and the development lifecycle — closed 16 September. E3 changes how the three descriptors are picked, never what they are or what is stored.

    How it would be verified at build

    • Unit: a source guard for the toolbar’s membership at ≤640, the 56px row and its three chip states, the dialog’s four answers and its docked foot, the “next unrecorded” rule including a scoped session, and the docked bar’s anchor.
    • The layout sweep on the practice plan, the session, the scoped session and the hub at 361 / 390 / 768 / 1440, plus two screens the sweep has never seen: the observation dialog open, and the session scrolled with the bar docked.
    • A hit-test, not a look, on the docked bar — but hit-test it in the states a coach is actually in. Probe the centre of the pill at rest and mid-scroll, at 390 and 360, and confirm the bar answers and not the bottom nav. ⚠ The game-day console’s own hit-tests missed a real defect because they scrolled to the page end first, which unsticks a sticky bar: a probe at a scroll position no coach ever reaches proves nothing. Run every probe again with a sheet actually open.
    • Check every fixed foot surface against the save pill. The autosave pill sits at 250 portal-wide, and its comment claims only the Schedule’s slide-over — so anything below 250 is drawn over by it, and in its error state it takes pointer events and can swallow the tap outright. A failed save in the field is exactly the moment this screen exists for. The portal’s convention for a sheet is 260 — above the pill, below the nav — the value the bottom-nav sheet anchor already uses.
    • The layout sweep reads the element, not its tap area — so every new target is measured at its own size. Anything drawn smaller than 44 must be an inner span inside a 44px element, never a small element wearing a big pseudo-element.
    • The CSS-selector gate before calling it done, not after. On the game-day build it caught three rules left with no caller and a comment asserting one of them was still used when it was not — a stale comment outlives the code it describes, and this stage deletes a control from the practice plan and two from every player row.
    • Driven by hand at 390 and 360: twelve players recorded end to end without scrolling once; the count on the bar after each save; Save & next player skipping an out-of-scope player; every row live at rest with nothing selected; the menu opening, closing on Escape and returning focus to its square.
    • A QA walk tab on this hub at build time, with its § number from the ledger.

    Walk practice week on a phone

    Forty-four steps in five parts. Tick each one as you go (they are remembered on this device), give each part a verdict, and paste the block back to me at the end. Everything below was verified on dev before this tab was written — every number in it was read from the browser's own geometry, never a screenshot — so the walk is to confirm it reads right to you, not to find out whether it works. Part D is the one that matters. It is the dialog a coach opens twelve times a practice, standing on a field, and until today its Save was 33px with four hundred pixels of nothing under it.

    ⚠ Three things I decided at build and want your read on — each is called out again at the step it belongs to.
    1. A skill row's state now reads Recorded rather than Saved, at every width. The chip could not say one thing while the row beside it said another — and the Review session table has read Recorded since stage 2, so the row was the odd one out on a desktop too, not just on a phone. A test row still says Saved, where an autosave really did land. (Step C3.)
    2. The session's title is not truncated. Removing the doubled date is the win; this fixture's session is named with a whole sentence, so it still takes two lines at 390 and three at 360. Clamping a title would hide part of a name a coach typed. (Step E4.)
    3. Clearing a descriptor on a phone is a second tap on the chosen answer. Four answers leave nowhere for the desktop's No descriptor, and a fifth row appearing the moment something is picked shifts the layout under your thumb. (Step D10.)
    ⚠ What “/review” changed after this tab was first written — worth knowing before you walk part D. Five lenses found four High defects, all of them mine, all in this dialog's new answer model, and two were data loss no automated gate in this repo could have seen — each needs a coach to make a specific pair of choices before it bites:
    1. A sentence typed beside Not assessed today was silently dropped. It now saves as that mark's own reason, which the row reads back — steps D12–D14 walk it both ways.
    2. The mark was cleared BEFORE the record was written, so a failed write left a player with neither while the dialog said “Not saved — try again”. The record is now written first and the mark cleared last; there is no transaction across two routes, so the ORDER is the whole fix.
    3. The answers claimed to be radio buttons and never implemented the keyboard pattern that claim owes — they are toggle buttons now, which is also what makes tap-again-to-clear honest.
    4. “Which answer is chosen” was two pieces of state that could disagree, so on one row the first tap cleared instead of selecting. It is one value now.
    Everything above was re-driven in a browser afterwards rather than re-read in code — which is how a fifth gap turned up that the review had not: the reason saved correctly but came back blank in a reopened dialog, so a coach could not correct it. Fixed too, and step D13 checks it.
    ⚠ One finding wider than this stage, deliberately NOT fixed here. No dialog footer anywhere in the portal has a phone or tablet tap floor — the buttons are ~33px in every sheet a coach saves from. E3 fixes this dialog at ≤640 because that was the ask, and the 641–768 band was ruled out of scope, so at a tablet width this same dialog still has its 33px Save. It is recorded in the layout baseline with that reason rather than swept in: fixing it properly moves every dialog in the product, and that wants a ruling of its own.

    D · The dialog — the stage's real deliverable

    1. Back on the skill, tap an unrecorded row. The dialog opens titled with the player and the skill.
    2. What did you see? is four rows you can hit with a thumb, each 56px: the three descriptors, then Not assessed today — quiet, and last. (It was a 37px native select: a tap, a wheel and a confirm.)
    3. The foot is docked at the bottom of the screen with no dead space beneath it. Save & next player takes most of the width; Save sits beside it. Both 56px. (It was a 33px Save floating mid-screen above 392px of nothing.)
    4. Tap an answer, then Save & next player. It opens on the next player who still needs recording — not simply the next row.
    5. Keep going. On the last player the “& next” button is absent, not greyed out — a button that says “next” never means nothing.
    6. Record all twelve this way without scrolling the list once. That is the whole point of the stage. (Verified on dev: the page's scroll position stayed at zero for the entire walk.)
    7. Now the mark's round trip. Open a row, choose Not assessed today, Save. The row keeps its chevron and its chip reads Not assessed.
    8. Tap that row again. Not assessed today is the chosen answer. ⚠ This is why a marked row had to stay a door — with the link off the row's edge it would otherwise be a one-way trip on a phone.
    9. Pick a descriptor instead and Save. The mark clears, and the row reads Recorded with the descriptor underneath.
    10. Tap a chosen answer a second time and it clears — there is no “none” row to hunt for. ⚠ This is the quiet gesture from the notes above. Tell me if you would rather have a visible No descriptor row instead.
    11. Selecting an answer shows a tick on it and thickens its label, not just a tint — the point being that it still reads in daylight glare and without colour vision. (A “/review” finding: the first build marked the choice by colour alone.)
    12. Choose Not assessed today and watch the field below RENAME itself to Why not? with a shorter limit. Type Left early — could not assess and Save. The row now reads that sentence beside its Not assessed chip. (The first build dropped it silently — this was the most serious thing “/review” found.)
    13. Reopen that row: the mark is the chosen answer and your sentence is back in the field, so you can correct it. Change it, Save, and the row shows the new wording.
    14. Now pick a descriptor on that same row and Save. The mark goes, the row reads Recorded, and your sentence carries over into the observation's own note — the field's label changed to Anything to add? when you switched, so you can clear it if you would rather. Nothing you typed is ever thrown away without you seeing it happen.
    15. A scoped session (Sessions → Phase 2 probe — scoped): players outside the plan are not in the list at all, and Save & next player skips anyone already recorded. (Verified: it carried the walk Avery → Blake → Casey → Frankie, skipping Devon.)
    16. On a desktop the dialog is unchanged: a Descriptor dropdown with No descriptor, a Cancel, and today's foot. ⚠ At a tablet width it is the desktop form too, 33px buttons and all — the wider finding in the notes above.

    E · The count follows your thumb, and one title

    1. The count and Review session → sit above the bottom nav, not at the bottom of the page. (They were at y=1,747 and y=1,801 on a 1,949px page.) The count changes on every save.
    2. Scroll the list. The bar stays, and the Review session pill is genuinely tappable there — not merely visible. (Hit-tested at rest and mid-scroll, at 390 and 360: the pill answers the tap, never the nav.)
    3. With a player marked, the bar reads “3 of 12 recorded · 1 not assessed”. The second clause appears only when a mark exists, so the word recorded never claims a mark is a record — and the figure is the same one the chip dropdown shows, so the screen cannot carry two counts that disagree.
    4. The page's title is the session's name; the date is on the when-line beneath it and nowhere else. ⚠ At 360 a sentence-named session still wraps — the second note above.
    5. Tap Review session →: the table and the names are exactly as before, and Done — back to Sessions still leaves.
    6. Open More → the More sheet while the bar is docked: the sheet opens over it, as every phone sheet in the portal must. (This is the check the game-day console failed when it over-corrected its own bar above the nav.)
    7. On a desktop the foot is the sentence and the button it always was — “4 recorded · 1 not assessed · 1 not recorded — of 6 in scope” — in normal flow, nothing pinned.

    docs/projects/active/COACH_MOBILE_EXPERIENCE_PLAN.md · created 19 Sep 2026 · the source file is the record; this tab renders it

    One stage at a time. Each stage: drawn at true size on this hub → owner rules (paste-back) → build prompt → build → /review → QA walk on this hub → owner QA → next stage. No stage starts before the one before it is ruled; a stage may be built before the previous walk is complete when the owner says so.

    0 · What this is

    A holistic re-evaluation of the Premium Coaches Portal at phone width, in the shape of the Practices and Skills & Goals re-evaluations: a walk of every screen a coach reaches on a phone in a game week and a practice week, measured; a set of shape questions for the owner; and a stage ladder, each stage drawn, ruled, built and walked in turn.

    What was measured (19 Sep 2026, dev, UAT head coach): 34 screens at 390×844, six at 360×780. Per screen: height in screens, words on the first screen, controls under the 44px tap floor, words at ≤11px, pinned chrome. Interactions driven: the More sheet, the Schedule’s three views and event sheet, a chat room, the live plan, the lineup grid, the console, the recording page, a roster row’s blank side. No sideways scroll at either width on any screen.

    PM brief

    Coaching from a phone

    docs/projects/active/COACH_MOBILE_EXPERIENCE_PM_BRIEF.md · 19 Sep 2026

    What we are proposing

    A staged re-shaping of the Premium Coaches Portal for phones — the way most coaches will actually use it in-season. Not a redesign: the screens, words, doors and data stay. What changes is the container each one sits in at phone width, so a coach with one thumb reaches the day’s tool in one tap and reads the day’s facts on the first screen.

    What a coach sees and does differently

    • More is a real sheet. Tap More and the whole menu rises from the bar — Practice plans, Lineups and Skills & Goals as the first three tiles — instead of a narrow list that scrolls inside itself.
    • One line says where you are. The team name and record sit in a slim line at the top of every screen; a chat room has one header, with back on the left. Stage 1 (ruled 21 Sep, built): a coach with more than one team switches by tapping the team name — a chevron opens a short sheet of their teams, and those rows left More; and every screen, the Overview included, wears the same one line, with the club and season in a quiet line under it on the Overview that scrolls with the page. Nothing jumps under the thumb, and the “?” never disappears.
    • The first screen fits the phone. Overview’s six tiles become six rows — the figure and one qualifier each, the whole row a door — and the game-day card’s two jobs become two full-width taps while its call time and kit join the facts line. Built 21 Sep: the Overview 948px against 1,104, all six rows above the bar at 390×844.
    • Schedule opens on today. The season so far folds above; week view skips empty days; month view shows dots and lists the day you tap; on game day the event opens on attendance and the lineup, not the score box.
    • Lineups start with the players. The setup controls fold into one line once a lineup exists; undo, redo, print and templates become one icon row.
    • Recording at practice is one tap per player. A player is a row; the dialog offers Next player; the tally and Review stay docked above the bar.
    • “Saved” stops sitting over the work. It appears only while something is saving and fades once it has; only a failed save stays, with its Retry.
    • The field is readable at arm’s length. The console’s positions and counts come up to body and support sizes.
    • Tables that fit stay tables. The attendance report is twelve rows, not twelve cards.

    Why it matters

    The portal was built desktop-first and adapted to the phone screen by screen; the adaptations are individually reasonable and cumulatively heavy — 131px pinned before content, a menu that hides half of itself, lists that open on April, a lineup whose first player is under the first screen. Coaches use this product at the fence. Every stage returns screen to the work and taps to the tool.

    Role-based differences

    None new. An assistant sees fewer doors in the sheet (the same gating as the sidebar); a viewer sees the read faces they see today. Nothing a coach cannot do today becomes possible, and nothing they can do today goes away.

    Trade-offs

    • Two layouts per screen where the phone diverges (rows vs tiles; folded vs open setup). Kept to the container, so copy and data have one source.
    • The bottom bar’s four tabs stay; the owner may swap Roster for a season tool after stage 2 if the sheet does not settle it.
    • Stage 5 (the player’s read face) waits for the roster and player page walk (§182).

    Priority and sequence

    Stage 0 first (the shell — cheap, and it lifts every other screen); then the first screen and the Schedule, which are the roads to everything; then game week, practice week, people, reports. Each stage is drawn on this hub, ruled by the owner, built, reviewed and walked before the next begins.

    Success criteria

    • Practice plans, Lineups and Skills & Goals each one tap from any screen.
    • Pinned chrome at rest ≤110px on every team screen but Overview; no screen with two stacked headers.
    • The Schedule’s first upcoming row on the first screen at 390.
    • The lineup grid’s first row on the first screen at 390 once a lineup exists.
    • No Saved pill at rest anywhere — it appears on an edit and fades after the save; no console text under 12px; the attendance report under 1,600px at 390.
    • The layout sweep green at 361/390/768/1440 on every touched screen, with the new field-floor rule.
